text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo newspapers this morning. - - -
-- NEW WATERWAY WILL REDUCE SOYBEAN PRICES BY 30 PCT
The cost of transporting a tonne of soybean out of Mato Grosso, Brazil's prime soyproducing region, has dropped from $105 to $70 a tonne thanks to the new Madeira-Amazon waterway.
-- IADB COULD LEND BRAZIL AS MUCH AS $1 BILLION THIS YEAR

Brazil could receive as much as $1 billion for infrastructure investment this year from the InterAmerican Development Bank, senior officials said. They said over $5 billion in funds have been approved and only require an equivalent amount to be deposited by Brazil's Federal government to be made available.
-- FRANCE AGREES TO DISCUSS FARM SUBSIDIES
French President Jacques Chirac said Thursday that France would support open agenda talks on farm subsidies to put an end to the war of words being fought by the European Union and the United States.
-- SEVERAL MEMBERS OF MAYOR'S OFFICE INVOLVED IN BOND SCHEME
At least five members of the Sao Paulo mayor's office were involved in a scheme that organized the issuance of judicial debt bonds for several states and municipalities.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso approved a plan put forward by the Forca Sindical labour movement designed to reduce the work week and seek new ways to create jobs.
COLLOR AIDE DID BUSINESS WITH COLOMBIAN DRUG TRAFFICKERS

Paulo Cesar Farias, President Fernando Collor de Mello's former campaign treasurer, forged links with Colombia's Cali Cartel and Italian Mafia bosses with an eye to develop new businesses in Latin America.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
